documents.label: Docket documents

Two payload fields are not carried: `comment` (the inline submission body) and `restrictReasonType` (why a document is withheld). Read those from the acquisition source, the raw Mirrulations payload or spicy-docs' source-native release, not from this table.
documents.coverage: Sampled repair with retained prior rows. On 2026-09-21 the fork merged every selected retained document release into the prior table, resolving each document to its most recent source record and keeping newer and unrelated rows; the daily regulations ETL adds to it. It is not a fresh regulations.gov census. The repair covered metadata and references; body-text, extraction-status and PDF-extraction-evidence values remain NULL. It does not include a full comments corpus. Receipts: fork-execution-2026-09-21/publication-documents.json and fork-base-repair-2026-09-21/repair-audit.json.
documents.data_quality: The 2026-09-21 fork date check across all 2,001,531 rows found 52,699 posted_date values before 1990, including eight in year 0000; one value was in the future, 2,020 were missing and no other values were uncastable. Source date values remain literal in this base table; downstream calendar filters are separate. Receipt: fork-execution-2026-09-21/document-derivatives/audit.json. In the 2026-09-21 fork consumer audit, 1,854,836 documents resolve to published dockets; 466 preserve unmatched literal links across 137 docket IDs, and 146,229 have NULL links. The 348 selected-source unmatched links and 145,907 selected-source NULL links agree with native inputs; the remaining 118 unmatched and 322 NULL rows are outside that replay. Missing joins are not fabricated or treated as failed repairs. Receipt: fork-execution-2026-09-21/documents-mcp-audit/.

Literal records from an explicitly read document attachment relationship, preserving attachment IDs, restrictions and alternative file formats. Null means the relationship was not read; an empty array means a validated complete read returned no attachments. A main document response alone cannot establish attachment absence.
Federal Register document number, when the document was published in the FR. Often null.
Whether the document was withdrawn, as the string `"true"`/`"false"`. Often null.
Agency-supplied reason for withdrawal, when withdrawn. Often null.

Plain text extracted from the document's PDF attachment(s) by the PDF text-extraction step. Null until that step has run; see `text_extraction_status`.

Aggregate PDF outcome: `ok` means at least one PDF supplied text, even if another failed; otherwise `error`, `encrypted`, or `empty` (no extractable text) in that order. Null before an attempt. See `pdf_extraction_results_json` for each file.

Ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL. comments.label: Public comments
comments.summary: One row per public comment — the largest table (tens of millions of rows). On R2 it is also published as Hive-partitioned files under `comments/agency/agency_code=.../part-0.parquet`, one file per agency, rebuilt daily — this is what `spicy-regs-ui` reads for scoped queries. (An older `comments/agency_code=.../docket_id=.../year=.../month=...` tree was abandoned when comments moved onto the Iceberg catalog and carried a reduced set of columns; prefer the per-agency tree.) Joins to `dockets` on `docket_id` when the source supplies that relationship. Comments with a null docket remain in the table and agency totals.
comments.coverage: True range, floored. Posted dates are stated from 1990-01-01 to 2026-09-06 rather than from the raw minimum of year 0000, on the same publisher defect as `documents`. See the data-quality note.
comments.data_quality: 33,373 rows carry a `posted_date` before 1990, the same publisher defect as `documents`. Filter on the date when recency matters.

columns.description: Unique comment identifier. Primary key / dedup key.
Source-supplied docket identifier for joining to `dockets.docket_id`. Null when the source does not identify a docket; mirror directory names and comment ID prefixes do not fill this field.

Literal Regulations.gov commentOnDocumentId: the named parent document, independently nullable from docket_id. No identifier-prefix inference. NULL where the row predates reading this field, which today is most rows, including every row of the largest agencies; NULL does not mean the comment names no document.
Literal commentOn in the native object-ID namespace; not interchangeable with a public document key.
Literal originalDocumentId, retained as an unresolved legacy source reference.
JSON map containing only present source parent-reference fields, preserving null and empty values. {} means the source was read and fields were absent; SQL NULL means legacy or unread.
Receiving agency's short code.
Commenter's first name, when provided. Often null.
Commenter's last name, when provided. Often null.
Organization the commenter represents, when provided. Often null.

Submitter category as classified on regulations.gov. Often null, and empty for whole agencies: EPA, for one, classifies submitters in `subtype` instead (Company/Organization, Government, Mass Mail Campaign, …) and counts campaigns in `duplicate_comments`.
Comment title / subject line.

Full free-text body of the comment as typed into the comment form; filled for nearly every comment. Text of attached files is in `text_content`, which is filled only where an attachment was extracted. The largest field in the dataset.
Document category for the comment record, typically `Public Submission`.
Date the comment was posted publicly (ISO 8601 string).
Timestamp the comment was last modified (ISO 8601 string).
Date the agency received the comment (ISO 8601 string).

JSON array of any files attached to the comment: `[{title, formats:[{url, format, size}]}]`, from the object's `included` attachments. NULL when the comment lists none, and also where the row predates reading them: the extract gained this column on 2026-03-15 and rows ingested earlier kept NULL, since the ETL rewrites a row only when its modify_date moves (about 2.3M such rows, estimated 2026-09-28 in mirrulations-field-census-2026-09-28/attachments_weighted.json, every posted year from 1996; cause proven in comments-full-reread-2026-09-28/attachments-root-cause/). The comment re-read fills them; until then NULL does not mean no attachments.

Plain text of the comment's attachment(s). Filled inline during the ETL from Mirrulations' own extraction (the bucket's `derived-data` prefix): one extraction tool per comment, its attachments in number order, each stripped and separated by a blank line; when that tool's objects are all blank there is no derived text. Attachments Mirrulations has not extracted are backfilled by the on-demand PDF text-extraction step. Null when neither has produced text; see `text_extraction_status`.

Where `text_content` came from, or why there is none. `derived` means Mirrulations' own extraction supplied it (see `pdf_extraction_results_json`); `ok` means Spicy Regs extracted text from at least one PDF, even if another failed; otherwise PDF outcomes prefer `error`, `encrypted`, then `empty`. Derived-data fills written before `derived` existed read `ok` until repaired. Null before an attempt or derived-text fill.

Provenance of `text_content`. For `derived` rows, a JSON object `{comment_id, tool, available_tools, attachments:[{attachment, tool, key, size, etag, sha256}], only_in_other_tools}`: the primary tool (the first of `pypdf`, `pdfminer` with an object for the comment), every tool with an object for it, each attachment's tool, S3 key, listed size and ETag and the SHA-256 of the bytes read (null when the text was kept without re-reading them), and the attachment numbers taken from a tool other than the primary because the primary has no object for them (decision 41); those are in the text. A primary object that exists is kept even when blank. About 125 bytes plus 330 per attachment (31 KB at 92 attachments, the published maximum). Otherwise an ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL; SHA-256 identifies observed bytes, and no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when neither is recorded.

The agency's own class for the submission (regulations.gov `subtype`), spelled as stated. It is agency-specific. EPA classifies the submitter: `Public Comment` (an individual), `Company/Organization Comment`, `Government Local`, `Government State`, `Government Federal`, `Government Tribal`, `Member of Congress`, `Mass Mail Campaign`, `Late Comment`. Most other agencies that state it put one generic label on every record (`Comment(s)`, `Public Comment`, FDA's `Electronic Regulation from Form`), and many state none. In a 2026-09-28 sample of 5,945 Mirrulations comments across 179 agencies it was stated on 2,041 records in 69 agencies; submitter classes appeared only at EPA, and `Mass Mail Campaign` also at EERE, BSEE, OSHA and TTB. Split organizations from individuals only within an agency that classifies, and not by `organization`: all 1,629 records of EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114 leave `organization`, `category` and `first_name` NULL, 219 of them `Company/Organization Comment`. NULL where the record states none or the row predates reading this field.

How many received submissions the agency says this posted record stands for (regulations.gov `duplicateComments`), as stated. Most agencies do not count and state 0 on every record; EPA states 1 for a single comment and the campaign's size on a `Mass Mail Campaign` record (15,851 on EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114-1811, National Wildlife Federation Action Fund). Rows are posted records. To estimate submissions, sum `GREATEST(duplicate_comments, 1)`, each posted record standing for at least itself, and first count the NULL rows: GREATEST reads NULL as 1. The sum is the agency's posted accounting, not its official total: EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114's 1,629 records sum to 53,707 (52,086 on 23 campaign records), while EPA's response to comments reports about 122,200 received. The 2026-09-28 sample found it stated on every record: 0 on 5,281, 1 on 660, more than 1 on 4. NULL where the row predates reading this field; 0 is a stated zero.

cfr_sections.label: Code of Federal Regulations sections
cfr_sections.summary: One row per GovInfo annual CFR granule, including sections, appendices, tables of contents and other structural units; metadata only, no regulatory body text. Neither a granule id nor a printed section number establishes the enclosing part, so each section granule is placed under the PART heading of its package's annual volume XML: Title 43 numbers sections by subpart (§ 1601.0-1 is in Part 1600), Title 41's parts contain a hyphen (`50-201`) and Title 14 Part 241 prints `19-8.1`. `part` is that structure; `cfr_ref` is the printed citation that joins the Federal Register side. Other granules keep the part their identifier spells, so Title 41's TOC and NODE rows keep parts cut at the hyphen (`50`). The Parquet footer key `spicy_regs.cfr_sections.placement` records that every row was placed by this rule; generations without it keep identifier-derived parts. A package is re-placed only when it is new or its GovInfo lastModified changed; an unchanged package, or one whose volume cannot be read, keeps its prior rows. Missing credentials and incomplete source traversals refuse before output replacement. GovInfo's annual index package (`GPO-CFR-INDEX-2025`) is not a title volume and is not in the table. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
cfr_sections.coverage: Window. Annual-edition section metadata from the 2025 and 2026 editions, not full publication history or body text. Each section's part comes from its volume's PART heading; on 2026-09-23 every compared Title 41, 43 and 14 section agreed with eCFR's 2025-01-01 structure. Receipts: fork-execution-2026-09-21/cfr-ancestry-fix-2026-09-23/ (candidate.json, validation.json).

columns.description: GovInfo granule identifier. Primary key / dedup key, including non-section structural units.
GovInfo package identifier for the enclosing annual CFR title and volume.

Join key to Federal Register `cfr_references_json`. For a section, the title and its printed citation (e.g. `43-1601.0-1`, `41-50-201.1`); Title 43 keeps its subpart-numbered spelling while `part` names the enclosing part. Title 41's compound-part citations do not join yet: the Federal Register side reads `41 CFR 50-201.1` as `41-50` (plan A7). NULL for ranges, publisher typos, unprefixed numbers (`Sec. 1-1`), parenthesized citations (`1.401(k)-1`), sections outside a numbered PART and section tokens the volume does not hold; 12 single sections printed with `§§` (`§§ 2.188`) are read as ranges until spicy-docs 0.31.0. For other granules, composed from the identifier's tokens (e.g. `48-700`, `15-746.10-app1`); NULL without a part.
CFR title number from the package or granule identifier (e.g. `40`).

For a section, the number in the enclosing PART heading of the package's annual volume XML (e.g. `1600`, `50-201`, `241`); NULL outside a numbered PART or when the volume does not hold the section. For a section's appendix or TOC (`sec746-10-app1`), its host section's part when the volume holds the host, else its token's leading number. For other granules, the identifier's part token including letter suffixes (e.g. `1203a`), which cuts Title 41's compound parts at the hyphen.

For a section, the printed number less its `{part}.` prefix (e.g. `1` for § 50-201.1, `19-8.1` in Part 241, `1601.0-1` in Part 1600, `401(k)-1`). For a section's appendix or TOC, the rest of its token after the leading number (`10-app1`); for a section token the volume does not hold, the whole token. NULL for other granules.
Granule heading / caption text from GovInfo's list-level `title` field.
GovInfo granule class / structural level (e.g. `CONTENT`, `NODE`, `TOC`, `APPENDIX`).
Annual edition year from the package or granule identifier, falling back to the year in `dateIssued`. This is not necessarily the printed body revision year or proof of a substantive edition.
Granule `lastModified` when supplied, otherwise the enclosing package's `lastModified`. GovInfo's granule listing supplies none, so in practice every row carries its package's stamp.
Canonical GovInfo details URL composed from the package and granule identifiers.

congress_bills.label: Congressional bills
congress_bills.summary: One row per bill or resolution. `bill-family` writes this table, filling the full contract for the Congresses it is scoped to (the current Congress on its daily schedule) — from a BILLSTATUS document for the 108th onward, and from the API bill detail route for the 82nd through the 107th, where no BILLSTATUS bulk exists. A consumer tells the two family routes apart by Congress and by the NULLs: a row for a Congress below the 108th is the detail route's, its `schema_version` is NULL because the detail record states no BILLSTATUS schema, and its `action_count`, `committee_count`, `version_count`, `subject_count`, `subjects_json`, `related_bill_count` and `related_bills_json` are NULL because the detail record states those only as sub-route counts the backfill does not walk — a zero would contradict the count the publisher declared. `cosponsor_count` is the one count the record does state, as its `cosponsors` sub-route's count, and is published from there (NULL when the record states no such sub-route, as the 92nd's do not). The BILLSTATUS route's separate count defect is described below. `stage` and `signed_date_rule` are NULL on these rows too: the record carries no actions, so no stage rule ran and no became-law action was looked for, and the shaper's default rung ("introduced") or the rule name "public law without a became-law action" would each be a statement about the bill that nothing examined. The first ten columns keep the exact order and spelling they have always had, because other repositories pin that prefix by digest; every new column is appended after them. Until plan A1 retired it (decision 31), a second rollup, `congress-bills`, walked the Congress.gov list route for that prefix across the whole archive, and a row of a Congress the family has not been scoped to keeps the prefix that walk last stated. Because rows from the two routes state different columns, this is the one table merged column-wise: a family row's NULL cannot erase a list-era value. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
congress_bills.coverage: True range on the archive index, mixed on enrichment. The archive index lists bills back to the earliest Congresses (latest actions from 1799-12-16); the bill family fills every column from GovInfo BILLSTATUS for the Congresses it has read, which begin at the 108th. On 2026-09-26 the 108th-117th rows, then written by a retired list walk, lacked 1,299 bills against the BILLSTATUS listings (199 in the 117th; receipt `join-gaps-2026-09-26/d/`); bill-family runs scoped to those Congresses fill them. An absent CBO element does not mean CBO never scored a bill. The bill family re-reads its own prior once where the CBO outcome is missing, or where a reader other than the running one read it, even when the publisher stamp is unchanged; a bill of the 82nd-107th filled from the detail route is re-read the same way, within the run's fetch cap. A bill the running reader found refused in, or dropped from, its folder's unchanged zip is not read again until the zip moves or another reader runs.
congress_bills.data_quality: **Known BILLSTATUS count defect in vendored SpicyDocs 0.24.2:** the `cosponsor_count` description below incorrectly treats cosponsors as sponsors after the first. The publisher lists them separately. A direct native-XML audit found 13,154 wrong zero counts in the retained 118th Congress HR/S output. The corrected local SpicyDocs checkout and offline candidate count every listed cosponsor, including withdrawn entries, but the normal vendored package and prior outputs have not adopted that fix. Receipt: `legislative-release-candidate-2026-09-21/`. `statutes_at_large_cite` is filled at this table's merge by joining the published `laws` table on `bill_id`, as its column sentence says: `bill-family` reads `laws` best-effort after its merge and takes the law's citation where one is published, keeping a citation already here where `laws` has none for the bill; with no `laws` table published the column stays as it was, NULL on a cold start. It is never guessed: `laws` publishes a citation only from a captured PLAW USLM file, and reads a NULL through its own `uslm_outcome`. `public_law_number` and `law_type` are not that case: they come from the bill's own publisher record — its `laws` entry, when the publisher states one — and are filled wherever the bill family has reached. `url_source` `congress_api_list` marks a row the retired list writer last wrote. Its run of 2026-09-23 replaced 3,044 BILLSTATUS `update_date` instants with the list route's same-day dates and 3,095 congress.gov page URLs with API resource URLs (receipt `drift-audit-2026-09-23/`). The bill family re-reads every such bill in its scope instead of skipping it as unchanged, so the current Congress's rows heal on its next run; the 47 rows it relabelled in the 114th–118th (five of the replaced URLs among them) are re-read only by a run scoped to their Congress. `update_date` merges by the larger value, so a re-read never moves it backwards; the 46 rows of the 119th (and 42 older) whose list date is later than BILLSTATUS's therefore keep that date-only value after the re-read, and until BILLSTATUS catches up they read `url_source` `billstatus` beside an `update_date` no BILLSTATUS document stated. `stage` reads a bill's actions in the publisher's order under spicy-docs 0.51.0, which moved 154,374 of the 172,991 stages with actions in its replay of the live generation (reproduced on 2026-09-29); a row keeps the earlier rule's stage until its Congress is re-read. The 26 BILLSTATUS bills of the 108th-111th and 117th that stayed in doubt after every read on 2026-09-29 list a printing twice or without a type, so their `version_count` exceeds their `bill_versions` rows.

Date of the publisher's own latestAction entry.
Text of the publisher's own latestAction entry.
The publisher's updateDate for this record; the merge prefers the larger value.
The publisher's own legislation URL for this measure.
The BILLSTATUS schema version the document declared (3.0.0 today).
The publisher's updateDateIncludingText, which moves when a text version posts.
The date the measure was introduced, as the publisher states it.
The publisher's single policy-area term for this measure.
Every legislative subject term the publisher lists, as a JSON array in publisher order.
How many legislative subject terms the publisher listed.
Bioguide id of the first sponsor the publisher lists.
Full name string of the first sponsor, exactly as the publisher spells it.
Number of items in the publisher's separate cosponsors list, including withdrawn entries; NULL when that list was not examined.
Action code of the actions[] entry the publisher's latestAction names; latestAction itself states no code, so the two are linked on date and text.
The publisher's actionTime on the latestAction entry.
Source-system code of that same actions[] entry.
Source-system name of that same actions[] entry.
How many action entries this document carries; the bill_actions row count for this bill.

How many committees and subcommittees this document names, at any nesting depth.  This is the bill_committees row count except where the publisher states a committee with no systemCode, which cannot be keyed and is refused.
How many text versions this BILLSTATUS document offers.  Not the bill_versions row count: a PDF twin and an upload are rows the publisher's own list does not name.
Public law number from the publisher's laws entry, when the measure was enacted.
The publisher's law type for the first laws entry (Public Law or Private Law).

NULL here on purpose: the citation is published on laws.statutes_at_large_cite, read from the PLAW USLM meta, and the host fills this column by joining laws on bill_id at merge time. The family build sees one BILLSTATUS document and its printings; the PLAW is a different package the laws rollup acquires once per law, so filling it here would fetch every PLAW twice or read another table's output, which the one-pass rule forbids.
Interpreted legislative stage, including failed/vetoed outcomes; enacted law is terminal.
Which stage rule fired, or NULL when no rule fired and the default stood.
The matched text pattern, publisher code or vote-result reading used by the named rule.
Position in the publisher's action list of the action the stage was read from.
Date of the action the stage was read from.
The full action text the stage rule matched against, never shortened.
Interpreted signing date, from the coded became-law action.
Which of the three signed-date rules produced that answer.
Position of the became-law action the signing date was read from.
The publisher's action code on that became-law action.
Interpreted money-bill kind, or NULL when no rule claimed the measure.
Which money-bill rule fired, or NULL alongside a NULL kind.
The rule's reason codes, unit-separator joined; BillTrax computed and then discarded these.
Fiscal year detected in the title, spelled FY plus the year.
Which of the twelve appropriations subcommittees the title names.
The referral signals the money-bill classifier was given, sorted and unit-separator joined; this is the classifier's input, recorded so a classification can be re-derived.
The publisher's short title, from the first titles[] entry whose titleType names a short title; NULL where the measure states none, which is ordinary.
Every relatedBills entry the publisher states, as a JSON array, with each one's relationship details nested; this replaces BillTrax's hand-set related_bill_id with the publisher's own fact.
How many related bills the publisher states.

BILLSTATUS estimate-block observation: NULL means unread; populated means estimate items were read; requested-empty:absent means no element; requested-empty:present-and-empty means an empty element; requested-empty:unexpected-shape:<shape> names an unsupported XML shape. These are observations of this document, never evidence that no CBO estimate exists. Populated items can still have unkeyable URLs, which the family records as refusals.

Who stated url, and so which kind of URL it is: billstatus (the BILLSTATUS legislationUrl, the congress.gov page), congress_api (the Congress.gov detail record's legislationUrl, the same page), congress_api_list (the Congress.gov list route's url, the API resource), or inherited (this observation stated none and a host merge kept an earlier observation's value; its lineage is that earlier source, not a fresh read). NULL when url is NULL or the row predates this label.
Source list state: absent, empty or populated; NULL means not read.

congress_bills.grain: One row per bill or resolution, as one BILLSTATUS document states it.

bill_subjects.label: Bill policy areas and legislative subjects
bill_subjects.summary: Subject assignments returned by Congress.gov or GovInfo BILLSTATUS, keyed by bill_id for a left join to congress_bills.bill_id. policy_area is one publisher category; subjects_json is a JSON array of legislative subject names, not separate bill records. The consumer trims and deduplicates names. All columns are VARCHAR, including subject_count. carrier and enriched_at record how and when the answer was obtained.
bill_subjects.coverage: Sampled; it grows each run and is not a complete subject census. From the 108th Congress every bill the bill family filled from GovInfo BILLSTATUS is copied from its congress_bills row; other bills from the 108th come from their folder's BILLSTATUS bulk zip, 32 folders a run, newest Congress first. Bills from the 93rd to the 107th, and bills whose BILLSTATUS file the reader refuses, come from the Congress.gov API with a key, up to 2,000 a run. No folder read and no API request, page or retry starts 20 minutes or more after the run began. A list-level bill in a folder the family reads waits for the family while its Congress is the current or previous one, and then goes to the API.
bill_subjects.data_quality: A missing row can mean pending, failed or outside the configured scope. An empty assignment can mean no assignments or that the source did not hold the requested bill; those outcomes are not separately represented in this table. Rows copied from the bill family are rewritten when the family's BILLSTATUS read changes; other answers are not asked again. The table does not retain the original response or its digest.

columns.description: Stable bill key shared with congress_bills.bill_id, such as 119-hr-1. Primary/dedup key; join by this identifier rather than title.
Publisher policy-area name after trimming, or NULL when the returned answer has no policy area.
JSON array of trimmed, deduplicated legislative subject names. An empty array alone does not distinguish unassigned from not held.
Length of subjects_json, stored as a decimal string; not a count of bills or independent source responses.
Source reader that answered: govinfo-billstatus from the 108th Congress on, congress-api below it or where the BILLSTATUS file was refused.
UTC timestamp when this retained answer was shaped, not the publisher's modification date.

bill_subjects.grain: One observed subject assignment per bill_id, with the latest retained answer replacing its predecessor.

unified_agenda.label: Planned agency actions
unified_agenda.summary: One row per Regulation Identifier Number (RIN) per agenda edition, ingested from the OIRA/OMB Unified Agenda published at reginfo.gov by `build_unified_agenda`. A Tier-1 rulemaking-lifecycle source: the upstream, forward-looking catalog of rulemakings agencies *plan* to pursue, keyed by the same `rin` that appears in `federal_register` (`regulation_id_numbers_json`). Primary / dedup key is (`rin`, `agenda_edition`). All columns are stored as VARCHAR; array-valued fields are JSON strings.
unified_agenda.coverage: True range: every semiannual Unified Agenda edition reginfo.gov serves as readable XML, from 199510 through the latest; agenda_edition names each. No edition is held for 2004 or for spring 2012. A rule has one row per edition that lists it, so count distinct rin, not rows, for a number of rules.

columns.description: Regulation Identifier Number (e.g. `2060-AV12`). The RIN join key to `federal_register`. Half of the primary/dedup key.
Short code of the agency that owns the RIN.
Full name of the agency that owns the RIN.
Title of the planned rulemaking.
Agency-written abstract describing the planned action. Often null.
Status of the RIN in this edition (e.g. `Active`, `Completed`, `Long-Term`).
Stage of the rulemaking in this edition (e.g. `Prerule`, `Proposed Rule`, `Final Rule`).
OIRA priority classification (e.g. `Economically Significant`, `Other Significant`, `Substantive, Nonsignificant`).

Semiannual agenda edition the row was published in, as `YYYYMM` (MM 04=Spring, 10=Fall). Half of the primary/dedup key. Every readable edition since 199510 is held, so filter to one edition, or count distinct `rin`, before counting rules.
Whether the action is a major rule, as reported by the agenda (e.g. `Yes`/`No`). Often null.
reginfo.gov publication identifier for this agenda entry, when present.
JSON array of planned and actual milestone actions with literal source dates and Federal Register citations. A date with day 00 has month precision; labels such as To Be Determined remain unchanged.
JSON array of CFR citations affected by the rulemaking. The join key to the CFR.
JSON array of legal-authority citations the agency cites for the rulemaking.
Earliest distinct calendar date derived from the timetable, or NULL when none is derivable. Source month-only dates (MM/00/YYYY) use day 01 here; timetable_json retains their original precision.

Second distinct calendar date derived from the timetable, or NULL when fewer than two dates are derivable. May be historical; it is not selected relative to today. Source month-only dates use day 01 here; timetable_json retains the literal dates.
URL of the entry's detail page on reginfo.gov.

rule_targets.label: Rule identity edges (docket, CFR, RIN)
rule_targets.summary: The rule-identity spine: one row per observed edge between a Regulations.gov docket, a CFR part and a RIN, with the `source` class of evidence that states it (docs/ontology.md, "The rule_targets carrier"). A missing or ambiguous reference leaves its target NULL rather than inventing one, and a `docket_document_cites_action_notice` row is a citation, with both targets NULL. Keyed (`docket_id`, `cfr_ref`, `rin`, `source`), NULLs included; joins `dockets` on `docket_id` and `unified_agenda` on `rin`. Built by `build_rule_targets`; all columns are VARCHAR.
rule_targets.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: `dockets`, `documents`, `federal_register` and `fr_docket_links` as the live snapshot's manifest pins them.

columns.description: Regulations.gov docket the edge belongs to, normalized; joins `dockets.docket_id`.
CFR reference the rule targets, `title-part` or `title-part.section` (e.g. `40-60`); NULL on a RIN-only or citation edge.
The CFR title of `cfr_ref` (e.g. `40`).
The CFR part of `cfr_ref` (e.g. `60`).
The CFR section of `cfr_ref` when it names one; NULL for a part-level reference.
Regulation Identifier Number the edge carries (e.g. `2060-AV16`); NULL on a CFR-only or citation edge.
The evidence class: `fr_cfr_ref`, `docket_rin`, `document_rin`, `document_fr_doc` or `docket_document_cites_action_notice`.
The least id of the records stating the edge: the docket for `docket_rin`, a dated Register record id (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`) for `fr_cfr_ref`, else a Regulations.gov document id.
Earliest Eastern day any evidence for the edge is dated, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
Latest Eastern day any evidence for the edge is dated, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
How the row was asserted; `deterministic` (computed by rule) throughout.
The builder that asserted the row, with its version (`spicy-regs:rule-targets:v<n>`), bumped when its published rows change.
The materialization run that built the snapshot (e.g. `rulemaking-20260927T062656Z`).
When that run asserted the row, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant.
Id of a prior row this one continues; always NULL here, since an edge has no id of its own.

JSON array of the literal Federal Register number references behind the edge, each with the `status` saying how it resolved (`dated`, `single_candidate_in_input`, `ambiguous`, `missing`, or a folded or unpadded match).

rule_targets.grain: One observed docket, CFR and RIN edge per evidence source class.

proceedings.label: Rulemaking proceedings
proceedings.summary: One row per rulemaking proceeding: the dockets that are one action, the Register documents that joined it, their stage events, RINs and CFR targets. A RIN names a Unified Agenda item, never a proceeding: it is carried as evidence and never groups dockets. A docket-less proceeding is one Register document. Keyed `proceeding_id`, which continues across generations when its dockets or Register documents overlap a prior one. Joined by `agenda_item_proceedings`, `comment_periods` and `rulemaking_lifecycles` on `proceeding_id`. Built by `build_proceedings`; all columns are VARCHAR, lists as JSON strings.
proceedings.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs (`dockets`, `documents`, `federal_register`, `fr_docket_links` and `rule_targets`) and the prior snapshot it continues ids from. A proceeding is docketed, or docket-less when it is a single Register document.

columns.description: Stable opaque id of the proceeding (`proceeding_<24 hex>`), continued from the prior generation where it overlaps one.
The proceeding's RIN when it holds exactly one, else NULL; a query aid, never its identity (`rins_json` lists every RIN).
JSON array of the Regulations.gov dockets the proceeding comprises; `[]` for a docket-less proceeding.
Title of its most recently dated titled document.

The agency code most of its documents carry. A docket-less proceeding takes its Register document's agency code. Each Register agency maps to one Regulations.gov code through RefSpec's agency projection and agency registry, whose identity bridges and successions give a defunct agency its current successor's code whatever the document's date: a 1998 Health Care Finance Administration notice is CMS. A split agency maps only when every successor gives the same one code. A department named with one of its own agencies yields to it (Transportation Department with FAA is FAA), and a department signing with one of its own unmapped bureaus keeps the department's code. NULL when no agency maps or the agencies are unrelated.
The one stage (`proposed`, `supplemental`, `final` or `withdrawn`) of its latest dated events; NULL when none, or when that day's events disagree.
JSON array of its stage events, one per staged document: `{effective_date, event_kind, evidence_id, joined_by, source, stage}`.
JSON array of the Federal Register document numbers it holds.
JSON array of the CFR references (`title-part`) that the `rule_targets` edges of its dockets name.
The same CFR references as Rulespec identifiers (e.g. `urn:rkaf:us:cfr:40:60`).
Always `[]`: legal authority belongs to the editioned Unified Agenda entry, never to an action.
How the row was asserted; `deterministic` (computed by rule) throughout.
The builder that asserted the row, with its version (`spicy-regs:proceedings:v<n>`), bumped when its published rows change.
The materialization run that built the snapshot (e.g. `rulemaking-20260927T062656Z`).
When that run asserted the row, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant.
The prior generation's `proceeding_id` this proceeding continues, so equal to `proceeding_id` on a continuing row (the id carries over); NULL for a proceeding new in this generation.
JSON array of the dated Federal Register record ids (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`) it holds.
How each `fr_document_ids_json` document joined, in the same order: `{fr_document_id, joined_by}`, `joined_by` being `fr_docket_link`, `fr_copy`, `specific_rin` or `fr_document`.
JSON array of Register number references it holds that resolve to no single record, each with its candidates and status.
JSON array of every RIN it holds, from its dockets, documents and Register documents.

proceedings.grain: One rulemaking proceeding: the dockets and Register documents that are one action.

regulatory_agenda_items.label: Regulatory Agenda items
regulatory_agenda_items.summary: One row per Regulation Identifier Number: the durable Regulatory Agenda item a RIN identifies, with how many proceedings evidence links it to and whether its scope is resolved. Keyed `agenda_item_id` (`urn:rkaf:us:rin:<rin>`), one per `rin`; joined by `agenda_item_proceedings` on `agenda_item_id`, and to `unified_agenda` on `rin`. Built by `build_regulatory_agenda`; all columns are VARCHAR.
regulatory_agenda_items.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: every RIN that `unified_agenda`, `dockets`, `documents` or `federal_register` states.

columns.description: The item's id, `urn:rkaf:us:rin:<rin>`.
The Regulation Identifier Number the item is (e.g. `2060-AV16`).
`recurring` (its latest Agenda priority is Routine and Frequent), `single_observed` (evidence links one proceeding) or `unresolved` (none or several).
Why `scope_status` holds: `latest_agenda_priority_routine_and_frequent`, `one_evidence_linked_proceeding`, `zero_evidence_linked_proceedings` or `multiple_evidence_linked_proceedings`.
How many proceedings `agenda_item_proceedings` links the item to, as a decimal string.
How many distinct Unified Agenda entries (edition and URL) list the RIN, as a decimal string; `0` when no edition does.
The latest Unified Agenda edition listing the RIN, `YYYYMM`; NULL when no edition does.
Earliest Eastern day any source dates the RIN: an Agenda edition or action date, a docket or document date, or a Register publication.
Latest Eastern day any source dates the RIN.
How the row was asserted; `deterministic` (computed by rule) throughout.
The builder that asserted the row, with its version (`spicy-regs:regulatory-agenda-items:v<n>`), bumped when its published rows change.
The materialization run that built the snapshot (e.g. `rulemaking-20260927T062656Z`).
When that run asserted the row, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant.
Id of a prior row this one continues; always NULL here, since an item's id is its RIN.
JSON array of unresolved Register number references from the Register documents that state this RIN.

regulatory_agenda_items.grain: One durable Regulatory Agenda item per RIN.

agenda_item_proceedings.label: Agenda item to proceeding links
agenda_item_proceedings.summary: One row per piece of evidence that an agenda item tracks a proceeding: a docket, Regulations.gov document or Register document that directly reports the RIN for that proceeding. Unified Agenda equality alone never links an action. Keyed `relationship_id`; joins `regulatory_agenda_items` on `agenda_item_id`, `proceedings` on `proceeding_id` and `unified_agenda` on `rin`. Built by `build_regulatory_agenda`; all columns are VARCHAR.
agenda_item_proceedings.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: `dockets`, `documents` and `federal_register` records that state a RIN the proceeding holds.

columns.description: Stable id of the link (`agenda_proceeding_relationship_<24 hex>`), from its RIN, proceeding, source and evidence.
The agenda item; joins `regulatory_agenda_items.agenda_item_id`.
The item's Regulation Identifier Number.
The proceeding the item tracks; joins `proceedings.proceeding_id`.
The link's role; `agenda_tracks_proceeding` throughout.
What reported the RIN: `docket_rin` (the docket), `document_rin` (a document's `additional_rins`) or `federal_register_rin` (a Register document).
The reporting record, by `source`: a docket id, a Regulations.gov document id, or a dated Register record id (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`).
Public URL of that record on regulations.gov or federalregister.gov.
Eastern day of the evidence: the docket's or document's latest date, or the Register publication date.
How the row was asserted; `deterministic` (computed by rule) throughout.
The builder that asserted the row, with its version (`spicy-regs:agenda-item-proceedings:v<n>`), bumped when its published rows change.
The materialization run that built the snapshot (e.g. `rulemaking-20260927T062656Z`).
When that run asserted the row, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant.
Id of a prior row this one continues; always NULL here.

agenda_item_proceedings.grain: One evidence record linking one agenda item (RIN) to one proceeding.

comment_periods.label: Public comment periods
comment_periods.summary: One row per notice's public-comment period. A notice is a Register record with the Regulations.gov documents whose `fr_doc_num` names it, or a Regulations.gov document the Register does not hold. Periods merge only on an explicit link: a notice whose title extends or reopens a comment period, and that names an earlier notice still open when it opens (by the page that notice starts on, or as the one open notice sharing its RIN), lengthens that notice's period; one that opens after the period closed starts its own. A docket or proceeding anchors a period (`anchor_kind`) and never merges two, and a Federal Register feed docket (`AGENCY_FRDOC_0001` and the like) anchors nothing. Keyed `comment_period_id`. Its proceedings, dockets and RINs are JSON lists, so it joins through them rather than by a column. Built by `build_comment_periods`; all columns are VARCHAR.
comment_periods.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: every `federal_register` record with a `comments_close_on`, every `documents` row with a comment end date, and every Register record such a document copies lands in exactly one period, anchored or not. Left out are windows that close before they open, placeholder closes (see data quality), and legacy Regulations.gov documents that state a comment end but neither a comment start nor a posting date (all closing by 2011); the builder logs each count. Live row counts come from `describe_table`.
comment_periods.data_quality: To find periods with a deadline in a date range, test all three date columns (`close_date`, `register_close_date` and `regulations_gov_close_date`): the two sources can state different deadlines for one notice, such as initial and reply comments (FCC) or written comments and oral or petition dates, and `close_date` keeps only the later. `close_date` is the latest close the period's own records state; `register_close_date` and `regulations_gov_close_date` keep each source's, and where they differ (Regulations.gov often holds a window open past the Register's date) the later one closes the period. A close on or after 2050-01-01 is a placeholder and states nothing: the inputs hold no close from 2033 to 2049, and every later one is a stand-in (Regulations.gov's 2099 and 2100 dates, FDA's 2050-02-21 open dockets, Register year typos such as 3008 for 2008). A record whose only close is a placeholder, or whose window closes before it opens, adds no dates; it is listed only as its notice's Register record when a copy states a window. The formal rulespec export is the anchored rows (`anchor_kind <> 'none'`), since rulespec's CommentPeriod needs a proceeding or docket anchor; no export exists yet. A Regulations.gov document is a notice's copy only when its `fr_doc_num` says so, so a copy that omits it stands as its own notice: on the 2026-09-28 inputs about 2,950 such documents share a docket, close day and opening (within three days) with a Register notice. An extension that names its notice by neither page nor RIN, or whose title says "extension of time for comments", stays its own period. A legacy Regulations.gov document whose posting date is decades early (see `documents`) opens its period that early.

columns.description: Stable id of the period (`comment_period_<24 hex>`), from the records that open it.
JSON array of the proceedings its notices belong to; `[]` when none resolves.
JSON array of the RINs its records state and its proceedings hold.

JSON array of the Regulations.gov dockets anchoring it: those its Register record names, else those of its copies, else a Regulations.gov notice's own; never a feed docket. `[]` where the publishers place the notice in no docket (the Register names none and no copy sits in one, as for FCC-2026-2942-0001), which is not proof that none exists.
Eastern day the period opens: the earliest opening among its records (a document's comment start, else its posting; a Register record's publication), `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Eastern day the period closes: the latest non-placeholder close its records state, the later of `register_close_date` and `regulations_gov_close_date`, `YYYY-MM-DD`. A deadline search tests all three.
The sources of the dates it takes, `+`-joined: `documents.comment_end_date` and `federal_register.comments_close_on`.
JSON array of public URLs of the records whose window opens the period on `open_date`.

JSON array of every record in the period, each in exactly one period: dated Register record ids (`number@date`), a notice's Register record included when only its copies state a window, and Regulations.gov document ids.

sam_entities.label: Federal entity registry
sam_entities.summary: One row per active SAM.gov registration, ingested from the Entity Management API v4 bulk extract (`/entities?format=json`) by `build_sam_entities`. The authoritative federal entity registry, the directory of organizations registered to do business with or receive assistance from the U.S. government, and the anchor for organization/entity resolution across the corpus: the same UEI ties a commenting organization to its registered identity. Filtered to public active registrations (`registrationStatus=A`); list-level fields only. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
sam_entities.coverage: Window, complete for the years read. Every public active registration SAM.gov dated 1996 through 2026 and the two older ones (1949, 1968), one bulk extract per registrationDate year: 792,846 registrations of 787,293 UEIs on 2026-09-26, against the entity API's 792,892 active that day. Each year matched its active count when read, less its credited renewals (see data_quality). Scheduled runs re-read the current year every other day and cycle through the older years between, and each year read replaces that year's rows.
sam_entities.data_quality: A row is a registration, keyed by `uei` and `entity_eft_indicator`: one entity registers once per EFT indicator (187 of the 147,038 UEIs in the 2026 extract carry more than one), so `uei` alone is not unique. SAM keeps a renewed registration's prior record Active until its expiry is processed, and counts both; the table keeps the newer, and the reader credits the other toward the file's declared count (one each in 2007, 2008, 2011, 2013, 2019 and 2020 and two in 2026, each journaled). A file with fewer registrations than it declares, less those credits, is refused. A year read retires the registrations it no longer holds (80 expired from 2002 and 2003 and 11 from 2026 on 2026-09-26), journaled as `rows-retired` so qualification reconciles every removal. A stalled extract is abandoned and triggered afresh, each abandonment journaled.

columns.description: Unique Entity ID (SAM `ueiSAM`, 12-char alphanumeric, e.g. `Q93HWX24PGA4`). With `entity_eft_indicator`, the registration key; alone, the entity-resolution join key.

Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code assigned to the entity. Often null for newly registered entities.

City of the physical address.
ZIP / postal code of the physical address.
U.S. congressional district of the physical address (`coreData.congressionalDistrict`). Null for non-US registrants.
Primary NAICS industry code the entity asserted (`assertions.goodsAndServices.primaryNaics`). Often null.

lobbying_filings.label: Lobbying disclosure filings
lobbying_filings.summary: One row per federal lobbying-disclosure filing, ingested from the U.S. Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) REST API (`lda.gov`, formerly `lda.senate.gov`) by `build_lobbying_filings`. Registrants file quarterly reports naming the clients they lobby for, the money involved, the issues raised, and the government entities (agencies/chambers) lobbied — so this table links the comment campaigns in `comments`/`dockets` to the same organizations' *direct* agency lobbying. Primary / dedup key is `filing_uuid`. All columns are stored as VARCHAR; nested/array fields are JSON strings.
lobbying_filings.coverage: True range: every filing of each filing year held, read whole from the LDA API, from the earliest filing year the backfill has reached to date; earlier years are added one year per dispatched run (owner decision 47). Query min(filing_year) for the current start.

columns.description: LDA filing UUID (e.g. `7866327b-c892-4430-b9f0-1f0f679c58c6`). Primary key / dedup key.
Filing type code (e.g. `RR` registration, `Q1`–`Q4` quarterly reports, `1A`–`4A` amendments, terminations). An amendment is a separate filing that restates its quarter's report.
Calendar year the filing reports on.
Reporting period within the year (e.g. `first_quarter`, `year_end`).
Timestamp the filing was posted to the LDA system (ISO 8601 string with timezone). Sort key.
Name of the registrant (the lobbying firm or self-filing organization).
LDA registrant id. Stable join key across a registrant's filings.
Name of the client the lobbying was performed for. Joins by name to `organizations`/comment filers.
LDA client id.

Lobbying income reported by a lobbying firm for the period, in USD. Null for self-filers (who report `expenses`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; keep the latest filing per registrant, client and quarter.

Lobbying expenses reported by a self-filing organization for the period, in USD. Null for firms (who report `income`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; keep the latest filing per registrant, client and quarter. A self-filing organization's expenses already include what it pays outside lobbying firms, whose `income` for that client is reported separately; do not add the two.
JSON array of lobbying activities, each `{general_issue_code, general_issue_code_display, description}` — the issue areas lobbied and their free-text descriptions.
JSON array of the distinct government entities lobbied (`{id, name}`) — the agencies and chambers (e.g. `HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES`, `SENATE`) named across the filing's activities.
URL of the filing's printable document page on lda.senate.gov (`filing_document_url`).

lobbying_activities.label: Lobbying activities
lobbying_activities.summary: One row per lobbying activity an LDA filing reports: the issue area, the registrant's description of what was lobbied, foreign-entity interests, and the government entities contacted for that activity. Keyed `(filing_uuid, activity_index)`, the position in the filing's own list, which is stable because LDA never edits a filing (an amendment is a new filing). Joins to `lobbying_filings` on `filing_uuid`. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
lobbying_activities.coverage: True range, the same filings as `lobbying_filings`: one row per lobbying activity a filing reports. A filing that lists no activity has no rows here.

The activity's position in the filing's list, from `0`. With `filing_uuid`, the key.

The issue area's name (e.g. `Science/Technology`).
The registrant's description of the specific lobbying, often naming bills (e.g. `S. 3597`).
The registrant's statement of any foreign entity's interest in the issue; often null.
JSON array of the government entities contacted for this activity, `{id, name}` objects (e.g. `SENATE`).

lobbying_activity_lobbyists.label: Lobbyists named on lobbying activities
lobbying_activity_lobbyists.summary: One row per lobbyist an LDA filing names on one of its activities, with the lobbyist's LDA id and name parts, any covered official position they held, and whether the filing lists them as new. Keyed `(filing_uuid, activity_index, lobbyist_index)`, positions in the filing's own lists. Joins to `lobbying_activities` on `(filing_uuid, activity_index)`. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
lobbying_activity_lobbyists.coverage: True range, the same filings as `lobbying_filings`: one row per lobbyist named on each activity. An activity that names no lobbyist has no rows here.

Nickname as filed; often null.
Middle name as filed; often null.

fec_committees.label: Political committees
fec_committees.summary: One row per observed Federal Election Commission committee. The current reader acquires from the unfiltered OpenFEC `/v1/committees/` endpoint through SpicyDocs; the delivered seed's selected scope is stated above. SpicyRegs preserves the existing 16 fields and JSON arrays, merges complete fresh traversals with prior observations by committee_id, and lets a fresh whole row replace its prior row. Raw page captures and acquisition manifests remain in FEC_CAPTURE_DIR. This identity/reference table can join other records carrying an FEC committee identifier. The company, union or association behind a PAC (FEC's connected organization) is not a column here: join `fec_committee_history` on committee_id and read `connected_organization_name`, one value per two-year cycle as that cycle's committee master states it (take the latest cycle for the current sponsor). All columns are VARCHAR; array-valued fields are JSON strings.
fec_committees.coverage: Not a range. The OpenFEC committee registry: the whole registry is walked every Sunday (decision 53) and committees that filed in the last week are read daily; rows only an earlier walk saw are kept. first_file_date and last_file_date describe filing activity, not acquisition.

Date of the committee's most recent filing (ISO 8601 string).

fec_collections.summary: Collection-level scope, counts and evidence for fec_source_records. Join collection_id to that table to distinguish observed records from empty results and uncollected populations. Join source_family to fec_source_catalog for the official access routes. Counts are stored as strings; cast explicitly for arithmetic.

The fec_collection_cycles view gives cycles stated by bulk directory URLs. This metadata does not establish complete official FEC history.

Provider reader profile: committee, candidate, filing, legal, audit, bulk, positional, agency, agency-document, postgres or document. NULL for caller disposition/context rows, which were not parsed by a provider profile.

fec_source_records.label: FEC source records with native metadata and evidence
fec_source_records.summary: Joinable metadata and retained source evidence across FEC families. collection_id joins fec_collections; source_family joins fec_source_catalog. Rows from different files and election cycles share this table, which has no cycle column: join collection_id to the fec_collection_cycles view for the cycle (2026 means 2025-2026) before comparing with a cycle's totals. A transaction's type, direction, other party, amount and memo flag are fields inside metadata_json (TRANSACTION_TP, OTHER_ID, CAND_ID, TRANSACTION_AMT, MEMO_CD). Native identifiers are lifted only when the provider reports them, and committee_id can join fec_committees. metadata_json and source_record_json preserve the complete provider record. PostgreSQL metadata additionally exposes named_fields from its verified schema; raw COPY fields, decoded NULLs and array text remain separate. Missing IDs remain missing.
fec_source_records.coverage: Sampled. The records of the selected collections in fec_collections, not complete FEC history. Inspect each collection's retained selection and source coordinates before combining observations. An archive's main file, date partitions and correction files can overlap; physical source rows are not a deduplicated transaction population.
fec_source_records.data_quality: Memo, subtotal and attribution fields retain their source meaning. Their eligibility depends on the source family, retained definitions and analytic purpose; no blanket memo exclusion applies to every query. Joint fundraising transfer and attribution observations can overlap without carrying an exact source link between them. Monetary values, amendment chains and record inclusion rules differ by family; generic record ingestion does not select a latest amendment or establish a safe sum. Unknown fields stay in native JSON. Original pinned bytes preserve numeric spelling where the provider exposes exact decimal values as strings.

columns.description: Selected collection label: the file or query the record came from. Together with source_record_id identifies this record; joins fec_collections.collection_id and, for the election cycle, fec_collection_cycles.collection_id.
Caller-selected official FEC source-family identifier, checked against the inventory. Joins fec_source_catalog.source_family; this classification is not independently inferred from source content.
Provider reader profile used to interpret the verified input.
Provider source-record identity, native API identity, bulk file key or byte-evidenced positional/agency-report observation ID, scoped to collection_id.

Committee ID as the source reports it (bulk CMTE_ID or the API's committee_id). In transaction files this is the committee that filed the report, not necessarily the one that received the money: a PAC's contribution to a candidate is filed under the PAC's ID, with the recipient in metadata_json OTHER_ID and CAND_ID, and TRANSACTION_TP says which way the money moved. Exact retained collection label. Join fec_collections in the selected source generation; the label alone is not a globally unique source identity.
Authority assigned to the selected source, preserving official FEC, unofficial originals and third-party research distinctions.
Captured source URL for this observation; it does not assert current availability or body retrieval.
SHA-256 of the original source witness bytes; distinct from the typed table's publication digest.
Digest of the sealed retained context object used by this mapping; separate from original-source bytes and typed output.
Exact JSON pointer into the retained collection context to the native fact represented by this observation.
Retained capture time value(s) as JSON without collapsing separately observed captures.
Type of retained CSV context row, preserving its source-specific population and meaning.
Literal FEC ID of the reporting committee where that source field identifies a committee. It does not by itself identify the sender or recipient of money.
Reporting committee name exactly as supplied by the retained CSV source.
The counterparty's name as reported, without a name-based identity merge.
Literal transaction identifier within its source filing/layout scope; not a globally unique transaction or economic-event key.
Literal source sub_id retained separately from typed identity and transaction ID.
Literal source value before conversion for amount. Preserves spelling, signs and empty values; the typed value and its status are separate.
Source-presence or conversion state for amount, distinguishing supported values from NULL, empty, missing or refused interpretation; it does not establish financial eligibility.
Literal date field of the retained CSV context row before source-specific interpretation.
Conversion state for the reported transaction/context date; distinguishes exact values, source NULL/empty and invalid or unsupported spelling.
Retained native field values for the source row or feed item, including fields beyond the typed mapping.
